entities.name: Infante Henry of Castile
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Infante Henry of Castile, known as "the Senator" (el Senador), was a highly ambitious and often disruptive Castilian royal, the fourth son of Ferdinand III of Castile and his first wife, Beatrice of Swabia. Born into the apex of Castilian power, Henry’s career was defined by a relentless pursuit of personal dominion, leading him into intricate political webs across the Iberian Peninsula, France, and especially Italy, where he briefly held the title of Senator of Rome. His life, spanning from an unknown birthdate to his death in 1303, encapsulates the volatile nature of medieval aristocratic ambition and the complex interplay between dynastic loyalty and personal gain in 13th-century European politics.

Henry’s early career saw him serve his brother, Alfonso X of Castile, but his true ambitions led him abroad. He first gained prominence in Italy, where he was lured by the papal promise of the Kingdom of Sardinia and later became a key figure in the struggle between the Hohenstaufen and Angevins. Appointed Senator of Rome in 1267, he initially supported Conradin, the last Hohenstaufen claimant, against Charles I of Anjou. His forces were decisively defeated and he was captured by Charles I of Anjou at the Battle of Tagliacozzo in 1268, leading to a 23-year imprisonment, first in Apulia and then in Castel del Monte, a stark testament to the high stakes of his political gambles. His release in 1291, secured by Pope Nicholas IV and large ransoms, allowed him to return to Castile.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Infante Henry's ambitious foreign policy and prolonged imprisonment shaped Castilian relations with other European powers, while his later regency contributed significantly to a period of political instability and factionalism during Ferdinand IV's minority, impacting the consolidation of royal authority in Castile.
